expect.note: 10,000 pages in a flat page tree; a run renders the first three, the middle and the last
5 pages: /Rotate 0, 90, 180, 270 and one that inherits 90 from the page tree
Negative-origin MediaBox, offset CropBox, CropBox with a quarter turn, CropBox reaching outside the MediaBox, reversed MediaBox corners
Every cross-reference offset is 13 bytes off; PDFium rebuilds the table
startxref points far past the end of the file
The first 62% of a valid file: no cross-reference table or trailer
A %PDF header followed by 2 KB of pseudo-random bytes
A 14400 x 14400 point page (the PDF maximum); rendered at a reduced scale to stay inside the pixel budget
6000 nested q operators before any drawing
36 blended and translucent layers
The 14 standard fonts, not embedded

Thirty levels of Form XObjects, each invoking the next three times, build 3^30 page objects while the page loads: the sandbox job runs out of memory and the engine is replaced (MemoryLimit). Seen on x64 on 2026-11-03, 6 s.

A tiling pattern with step 0.0001 pt filled over a 14400 pt page keeps PDFium inside one drawing operation, past any deadline. The request goes unanswered, the watchdog kills the engine as hung and the supervisor replaces it. Did not finish in 200 s on x64 on 2026-11-03; whether it ever ends is not known.

excluded.reason: Looked at 2026-11-03: 1,077 PDFs (156 MB) and 462 `.link` files that point at external downloads. The folder has no licence or provenance file at all; the files came from bug reports and web pages. The repository's Apache-2.0 licence is not evidence that each file may be redistributed, so none is included. Taking only the files whose origin can be shown (for example files pdf.js developers generated) would mean reading each commit; not done.

Included in the core tier as a sample (up to one pass and one fail file per clause directory, filtered by the font and producer rules in tests/corpus/curation). Left out: the `Isartor test files` folder (204 files, a separate suite whose licence the repository does not state), `TWG test files` (85) and `Undefined` (10) (no provenance stated per file), files over 1 MB, and files that embed proprietary font programs. About 2,350 other files were not sampled: most are near copies of the ones that were.

All 38 PDFs are CC BY-SA 4.0. ShareAlike is not on the list ADR-0010's amendment allows (BSD, Apache, MIT, CC0, public domain, CC BY). Nothing is adapted or redistributed here (the files are only fetched), so allowing ShareAlike later would cost nothing but the decision.

The PDF Association publishes these PDF 2.0 examples under CC BY-SA 4.0 (LICENSE.md). ShareAlike is not on the allowed list. (The same association's pdf-differences and safedocs repositories are Apache-2.0 and are included.)

samples/README says the files "can be distributed freely but does not come with explicit licensing terms or source files", and credits third parties (an IRS form, the US Copyright Office, a Japanese gazette, two research papers, iText). No licence, so none is included; only samples/contrib/matplotlib.pdf has one ("released under the terms of the LICENSE file") and a single file was not worth a source.

507 PDFs (260 MB) under pkg/testdata and pkg/samples. The samples are made by pdfcpu from its test inputs, some of which are third-party documents (the folder has a licence file only for its fonts). No per-file provenance, so none is included.

Ghostscript is AGPL-3.0, which ADR-0003 forbids; its public repository has no separate test-file licence, and its larger PDF test set is private. qpdf (Apache-2.0) is included: 330 of its 637 qtest files after the font, producer and duplicate rules.
Not examined. Apache PDFBox is Apache-2.0, but many of its test PDFs are attachments from JIRA issues with no per-file record of who granted what. Left for a later pass.
